children: , the global payments network, gained about 0.3% to $362.95 Wednesday morning as it teamed up with Reap to bring stablecoin-linked credit card programs to more than 100 markets. The pitch is simple: let businesses use stablecoins to fund card spending while merchants continue to accept Visa payments.

Reap handles the card processing, compliance and day-to-day operations. It already settles its Asia-Pacific obligations with Visa directly in stablecoins, and the companies plan to explore payments made by AI agents within limits set by users. That AI work is still an exploration, according to The Paypers , rather than a launched product.

Visa's $362.95 share price sits 10.15% below the $403.96 GF Value shown in the image. That gap gives investors a valuation reference, but the Reap announcement offers no forecast for card spending or additional Visa revenue. The test now is whether these programs bring meaningful payment volume onto Visa's network.

title: Visa Edges Up Nearly 0.3% as Stablecoin Cards Reach 100-Plus Markets
